clue.text: Dead bodies upset poor niece — not doing as told

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for dead, as on gravestones and in records

indicators.note: upset means the letters of the word bodies are knocked over into a new order
poor suggests the word niece is in a bad shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Corpses have distressed a hard-up young relative who never does what she is told.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals work here: 'upset' on the bodies and 'poor' on the niece, with the abbreviation for dead in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to follow orders is the very meaning of the noun, which names a failure to obey.

clue.text: Desperate doctor joins wine clubs

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
C is the card-game abbreviation for the suit of clubs

explanation.surface: A frantic physician signs up for wine societies.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate measures and extreme ones are the same thing, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Part of Russia is upset over old police chief

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece on top of the second
in a down clue, upset means the word is is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police, the NKVD

explanation.surface: A region of Russia is disturbed by a former head of the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Lavrentiy Beria ran Stalin's secret police; 'upset' turns the little word upside down in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast region east of the Urals forms most of Russia's land area.

clue.text: Pierced body a teen's sporting

indicators.note: sporting suggests the letters are frolicking about, so body, a and teen are mixed up

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A young person's body shows off piercings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of teen's adds no letter; BODY A TEEN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabbing someone with the blade fixed to a rifle is piercing them with it.

clue.text: Went by car from Dover, mistakenly

indicators.note: mistakenly means the letters of Dover are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone motored away from the Kent port of Dover by error.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the English Channel port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Going somewhere at the wheel of a car is the past tense of the verb to drive.

clue.text: Anger over rate charged in part of Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the synonym for anger is turned over, reading upwards

parts.note: ire means anger

indicators.note: charged suggests the letters of rate are energised into a new order

explanation.surface: Fury at the price levied somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IRE into ERI; 'charged' turns RATE into TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: This Horn of Africa country sits on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Composer coming up sick at heart

parts.note: the core of something is its heart

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the synonym for sick is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A musician on his way up feels sad deep inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns ILL into LLI, placed under CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist who wrote concerti grossi.

clue.text: Nightly broadcast?

parts.note: read as a homophone, nightly said out loud is knightly, which describes the gallant manner of a medieval knight

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a TV show every night; the sound of 'nightly' is 'knightly', and knightly behaviour is gallant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a knight means acting with courtesy and gallantry.

clue.text: Leader in school has to decapitate lad

parts.note: to head a plant or tree is to cut its top off, so head can mean decapitate
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A school prefect must chop off a youngster's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior pupil chosen to lead a school's boys is given this title in British schools.

clue.text: Greek character is prepared to grab computer

indicators.note: to grab means the outer piece seizes the computer and holds it inside

parts.note: on can mean ready to go, as in a challenge that is on
a micro is a microcomputer

explanation.surface: A Greek fellow is ready to snatch a laptop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is prepared' reads as a verb phrase, but it gives the two-letter word for ready, as in 'the game is on'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the short O.

clue.text: Close articles worn by idiot -when retiring?

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase pointing at garments worn when going to bed

parts.note: nigh means close or near

indicators.note: worn by means the articles sit around the idiot, as clothes around the wearer

parts.note: the is the definite article, so several of them can be written as plural thes
a clot is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool wears garments tight to his body as he goes to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives the plural of the definite article. 'when retiring?' defines by example: what one wears when going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightgowns are the garments put on for bed, which is what retiring means here.

clue.text: Experienced animal doctor hurried to cover mouse's tail

indicators.note: to cover means the two outer words wrap around the tail letter, holding it between them

parts.note: a vet is a veterinary surgeon, an animal doctor
ran means hurried

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A seasoned vet rushed to treat a mouse's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' has the vet and the running together wrap the last letter of mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An old hand with long service is experienced, an adjective and a noun alike.

clue.text: It could prevent sound reaching listeners on both sides of the piano

indicators.note: on both sides of means the two listeners flank the piano, one each side

parts.note: an ear is a listener
lug is slang for an ear, another listener
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A device stops noise from a piano reaching the ears of people beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listeners' gives two words for ears, EAR and LUG (slang), which flank P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pushed into the ear canal blocks noise, which is what this stopper does.

clue.text: Leaders from London University taking on US intelligence woman

indicators.note: leaders from means the first letters of London and University are taken

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: Heads of a London college sign up American spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucia is a female given name, so the answer is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Drummer and pianist one dismissed after short time

indicators.note: after places the shortened word for time first in the answer
short means the word time loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before cutting

indicators.note: dismissed means the letter for one is sent out of the word pianist

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drummer and a pianist, one of them sacked after a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TIME to TIM; 'dismissed' takes I out of PIANIST for PANIST.
explanation.definitionFit: This orchestral player beats the kettledrums, so is a drummer.

clue.text: Verse lines in pottery — making them smaller?

indicators.note: in means verse and lines are placed inside the word for pottery

parts.note: Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty
an ode is a poem, a piece of verse
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL means lines

explanation.surface: Poetry is written into the ceramics, and asks whether that shrinks them.
explanation.walkthrough: Ming porcelain stands for pottery; the definition plays on modelling as making small-scale copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Building a scale replica of something reproduces it in miniature.

clue.text: Bad with workers, and dismissive?

parts.note: food gone off is bad
handed means having hands, i.e. supplied with workers, as in short-handed

explanation.surface: A boss is poor at handling staff and brushes them off.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt, casual manner that shows no regard for others is brusque and dismissive.

clue.text: Was at peak, see, when tucking into apples etc

indicators.note: when tucking into means the word for see is placed inside the word for apples etc

parts.note: apples and their like are fruit
lo means see or behold

explanation.surface: Someone at their prime is told to look while eating apples.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word means he or she flourished, used of the peak working years of a person whose dates are unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin verb means flourished, the time someone was most active.

clue.text: Worker with current information for a toxin

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
I is the symbol for electric current
gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: An employee with the latest news about a poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign substance such as a poison that provokes the body's immune response is called this.

clue.text: She will fire projectile

definitions.meaning: a projectile fired from a gun

explanation.surface: A woman intends to launch a missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of a female pronoun and will, and an artillery round fired from a gun.

clue.text: Half-hearted response natural from Middle Eastern type

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase; the answer is the adjective for such peoples

parts.note: half-hearted means only partly, as the prefix semi- does
a tic is an involuntary twitch, a natural response of the body

explanation.surface: A lukewarm reaction comes naturally from someone from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMI means partly; TIC is an involuntary twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes peoples speaking languages such as Hebrew and Arabic, from the Middle East.

clue.text: The way over and around territory is taking forever

indicators.note: around means the reversed way surrounds the territory
in a down clue, over means the word for way is turned upside down

parts.note: a lane is a way or road
Ter is an abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: The road over and around a region takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the way upside down in this down entry, and that reversed road wraps the territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting without end, as something that takes forever does.

clue.text: Fast mover to score thrillingly

indicators.note: thrillingly suggests excitement that throws the letters of to score into a new order

explanation.surface: A speedster scores goals in exciting style.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor scooter or kick scooter zips along, so it is something that moves fast.

clue.text: Take to Russian river in the country

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
the Ural is a river in Russia

explanation.surface: Head for a river in Russia, out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: R comes from Latin 'recipe', meaning 'take', written on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural places are those away from towns, out in the countryside.

clue.text: Radiant young sheep went without first of wool

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep

indicators.note: without means the letter that follows is removed from the word went
first of means the opening letter of wool is taken

explanation.surface: A glowing lamb wandered off minus a bit of its fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: W (first of wool) is taken out of WENT, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle glow playing over a surface, like soft light, is described by this word.

clue.text: Describing no grey characters around university?

definitions.text: Describing no grey characters around university?

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the university abbreviation
characters means the letters of no grey are treated as a set to be reordered

explanation.surface: Students without grey hair are those of lesser age.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NO GREY, rearranged, go around U. Read as a whole, the clue describes people with no grey hair at college.
explanation.definitionFit: People of fewer years have not yet gone grey, which the comparative adjective describes.

clue.text: Strong popular number associated with south-east

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A powerful hit song is linked to the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings or heat are powerful and concentrated.

clue.text: Racy unorthodox theologian getting about with Liberal

indicators.note: getting means the anagram takes in the letter for about
unorthodox means the letters of theologian are arranged in a non-standard way

parts.note: c is the abbreviation for circa, about

explanation.surface: A risque heretical churchman is in cahoots with a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racy' looks like risque, but means relating to race. 'unorthodox' turns THEOLOGIAN into ETHNOLOGIA, which takes in C.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of peoples and races is ethnology, so its adjective means relating to race.
